shortDefinition: A thing or type that can be transformed.

themeExplanation.data: A kind of data, like a Raw CSV or a Clean Table — the stuff that flows between machines.
themeExplanation.alchemy: A kind of material, like Ore or an Ingot — the stuff your apparatuses work on.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: A kind of essence, like a Spark or a Flame — the stuff your runes act upon.
themeExplanation.abstract: A labelled point in a diagram, written A, B, C.

formalDefinition: In a category, an object is one of the things between which morphisms are drawn. It carries no internal structure of its own here — it is identified only by its name and the arrows into and out of it.
programmerAnalogy: A type, like A in a signature f: (input: A) => B.

shortDefinition: A process from one object to another.

themeExplanation.data: A machine that turns one kind of data into another, like a Parser from Raw CSV to Clean Table.
themeExplanation.alchemy: An apparatus that turns one material into another, like a Smelter from Ore to Ingot.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: A rune that turns one essence into another, like Ignition from Spark to Flame.
themeExplanation.abstract: A directed arrow f from a source object to a target object.

formalDefinition: A morphism f: A → B is a directed arrow with a single source object A and a single target object B. It need not be a set-function; what matters is that it has one source and one target and can be composed with other arrows.
programmerAnalogy: A function signature from one type to another: f: (input: A) => B.

shortDefinition: Chaining processes so the output of one feeds the next.

themeExplanation.data: Run one machine, then feed its output into another — a longer pipeline made of smaller steps.
themeExplanation.alchemy: Run one apparatus, then feed its output into another — a longer process made of smaller steps.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: Cast one rune, then feed its result into another — a longer working made of smaller steps.
themeExplanation.abstract: Follow one arrow, then another, to get a single combined arrow.

formalDefinition: If f: A → B and g: B → C, their composite g ∘ f: A → C is the single arrow you get by doing f first and then g. Composition requires the target of f to match the source of g.
programmerAnalogy: Combining functions: const gf = (x: A) => g(f(x)).
notationExamples: g ∘ f means do f first, then g.

shortDefinition: A do-nothing step from an object back to itself.

themeExplanation.data: A Pass Through machine that returns data unchanged — still a valid step in the pipeline.
themeExplanation.alchemy: A Preserve apparatus that returns a material unchanged — still a valid step.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: An Echo rune that returns an essence unchanged — still a valid step.
themeExplanation.abstract: The identity arrow on A, which leaves A as itself.

formalDefinition: For every object A there is an identity morphism id_A: A → A. Composing it with any arrow leaves that arrow unchanged: f ∘ id_A = f and id_B ∘ f = f for f: A → B.

shortDefinition: Different routes with the same start and end that give the same result.

themeExplanation.data: Two different pipelines that begin and end with the same data and produce the same output.
themeExplanation.alchemy: Two different processes that begin and end with the same material and produce the same result.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: Two different workings that begin and end with the same essence and produce the same result.
themeExplanation.abstract: Two paths with the same source and target that are declared equal.

formalDefinition: A diagram commutes when any two paths sharing the same start and end object are equal as morphisms. For a square with f: A → B, g: B → C, h: A → D, k: D → C, commuting means g ∘ f = k ∘ h.
programmerAnalogy: Two different implementations that pass exactly the same tests.

shortDefinition: Composing with a do-nothing step changes nothing.

themeExplanation.data: Putting a Pass Through before or after a machine gives the same result as the machine alone.
themeExplanation.alchemy: Putting a Preserve before or after an apparatus gives the same result as the apparatus alone.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: Putting an Echo before or after a rune gives the same result as the rune alone.
themeExplanation.abstract: Composing a morphism with an identity arrow leaves it unchanged.

formalDefinition: Identity morphisms are two-sided units for composition: for every f : A → B, f ∘ id_A = f and id_B ∘ f = f.
programmerAnalogy: f(id(x)) === f(x) and id(f(x)) === f(x), where id = x => x.

shortDefinition: How you group a chain of steps doesn't change the result.

themeExplanation.data: Whether you pre-bundle the first two machines or the last two, the pipeline behaves the same.
themeExplanation.alchemy: Whether you pre-bundle the first two apparatuses or the last two, the process behaves the same.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: Whether you pre-bundle the first two runes or the last two, the working behaves the same.
themeExplanation.abstract: Re-parenthesizing a chain of morphisms does not change the composite.

formalDefinition: Composition is associative: for f : A → B, g : B → C, h : C → D, (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f). So chains can be written h ∘ g ∘ f without parentheses. Identity + associativity are exactly what make objects and morphisms a category.
programmerAnalogy: compose(compose(h, g), f) === compose(h, compose(g, f)).

shortDefinition: A process that undoes another, returning to the start.

themeExplanation.data: Decode is the inverse of Encode — running both, in either order, leaves the data unchanged.
themeExplanation.alchemy: Cast is the inverse of Grind — running both, in either order, leaves the material unchanged.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: Read is the inverse of Etch — running both, in either order, leaves the essence unchanged.
themeExplanation.abstract: g is the inverse of f when composing them either way gives an identity.

formalDefinition: An inverse of f : A → B is a morphism g : B → A with g ∘ f = id_A and f ∘ g = id_B. When it exists it is unique, written f⁻¹.
programmerAnalogy: decode = encode⁻¹: decode(encode(x)) === x and encode(decode(y)) === y.

shortDefinition: A reversible process; its objects are the same up to renaming.

themeExplanation.data: A machine with an inverse — the two data shapes hold exactly the same information.
themeExplanation.alchemy: An apparatus with an inverse — the two materials are freely interconvertible.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: A working with an inverse — the two essences are freely interchangeable.
themeExplanation.abstract: A morphism with a two-sided inverse; the objects are interchangeable.

formalDefinition: An isomorphism is a morphism f : A → B that has an inverse. Then A and B are isomorphic, written A ≅ B. Isomorphisms compose, and ≅ is an equivalence relation on objects.
programmerAnalogy: A lossless, invertible transformation (a bijection between the two types).

shortDefinition: A structure-preserving map from one category to another.

themeExplanation.data: A way to copy a whole world of types and functions into another — like List, which turns each type into a list and each function into map of it.
themeExplanation.alchemy: A way to copy a whole world of materials and apparatuses into another — like Bundle, wrapping each in a set and each process into a per-element form.
themeExplanation.spellcraft: A way to copy a whole world of essences and runes into another — like Set, wrapping each in a collection and each working into a per-element form.
themeExplanation.abstract: A map F sending objects to objects and morphisms to morphisms, preserving the category's structure.

formalDefinition: A functor F : C → D assigns to each object A an object F(A) and to each morphism f : A → B a morphism F(f) : F(A) → F(B), such that F(id_A) = id_F(A) and F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f). It carries every commuting diagram in C to one in D.
programmerAnalogy: A type constructor with a lawful map, e.g. List or Optional.
